learning_objective: 🎯 Give your programs a brain! Learn how to make Python evaluate conditions and choose different paths using if-else statements.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: निर्णय (तय करना कि क्या करना है)
शर्त (जो True या False हो सकती है)
इंडेंटेशन (लाइन की शुरुआत में खाली जगह)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An `if` statement checks a condition. If the condition is True, it runs the code block inside it. If it is False, Python simply skips that block and moves on.

Unlike other languages that use brackets `{}`, Python uses spaces (indentation) to group code. Everything indented under an `if` statement belongs to that statement. Forgetting to indent causes an `IndentationError`.
Use `if-else` for two choices (If it is raining, take an umbrella, ELSE wear sunglasses). When you have multiple choices, use an `if-elif-else` ladder to check multiple conditions one by one.
Conditions are built using Relational operators (`>`, `<`, `==`, `!=`). You can combine multiple conditions using Logical operators (`and`, `or`, `not`).

fun_activity.title: 🎢 Rollercoaster Check
fun_activity.instructions: Write a mental code: `if height > 120: print("You can ride!") else: print("Sorry, too short!")`. This simple logic is exactly how self-checkout machines, ATMs, and game logic operate in the real world!

exam_tips: 📌 Always remember the colon `:` at the end of an `if`, `elif`, or `else` line. This tells Python that an indented block is starting.
📌 Do not confuse `=` (assignment operator, puts value in a variable) with `==` (relational operator, checks if two values are equal).
📌 In an `and` operation, BOTH conditions must be True. In an `or` operation, AT LEAST ONE condition must be True.
quick_recap: ⭐ The flow of a basic program is sequential (line by line). Decision-making alters this normal flow.
⭐ An `else` statement never has a condition next to it; it acts as a catch-all for anything that didn't match the previous `if` or `elif`.
⭐ Nested `if` means putting an `if` statement inside another `if` statement.
